summary: The exact candidate fixes the previously reported zero-argument super() failure and its focused tests pass, but it is only a partial hot-reload implementation. Independent adversarial cases show that deleted module definitions remain executable and that an edited class inheritance hierarchy remains stale for preserved classes and instances. The optional fault-tolerant serving loop is also not implemented. Request changes so unsupported source edits are either applied correctly or rejected explicitly rather than reported as successful.

tests.what_was_measured: Original feature absence on the prepared recorded base; import failed with ModuleNotFoundError.
Candidate regression suite, including preservation of an existing inherited instance whose updated method uses zero-argument super(); 6 passed.

Independent pure-Python reload behavior. The named super() regression passed, but deleted definitions remained present and callable, and changing Child(BaseA) to Child(BaseB) retained BaseA and produced the wrong result.

gpu_execution.evidence: The pinned interpreter reports torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2, HIP 7.2.26015, and torch.cuda.is_available() true, but this review did not execute a model server or GPU graph capture. Pure-Python counterexamples are sufficient to disprove full reload correctness; no startup smoke is claimed as serving-path proof.

native_rebuild_evidence: No C++, CUDA/HIP, FlyDSL, or other native source differs in the candidate; repository-environment.json also records native and wheel as null. A native rebuild was not applicable.
remaining_counterexamples: When a loaded selected module removes a top-level function or class, importlib.reload retains the old name in the module dictionary. reload_modules reports success, and the deleted function remains callable with stale code.

When a loaded selected module changes an existing preserved class from Child(BaseA) to Child(BaseB), _replace_class_contents does not update old Child.__bases__. Existing and new instances of the exposed preserved class continue through BaseA while the endpoint reports success.
remaining_limitations: The original issue's optional fault-tolerant scheduler event-loop behavior is not implemented.

Actual HTTP serving, weight preservation, target/draft graph recapture, and request drain/resume were not independently executed in this review; the available GPU does not by itself verify those paths.
Multi-rank TP/PP/DP/EP coordination was not exercised and requires a distributed architecture allocation.
Native extensions, new modules, object-layout/topology changes, torch.compile artifacts, JIT kernels, and arbitrary descriptors remain outside the candidate's supported scope.
Reload is non-transactional when module execution or a later worker fails.
